item.text: {"chapter_id":"4B","answers":[{"question_id":"4B.1","answer":"The evidence supports formal electoral competition but not reliably genuine contestability. Elections occurred on schedule, broad party registration was allowed, diaspora voting was piloted, citizen observers participated, the Constitutional Court validated 26 presidential candidacies and reinstated two candidates, and CENI commissioned a mixed national-international register audit that declared the register reliable. [BATCH-0001-E012, BATCH-0001-E015, BATCH-0005-E005, BATCH-0023-E015, BATCH-0027-E001] Against this, observers reported under-registration, incomplete or nontransparent auditing, conflicting voter totals, duplicated polling stations, late or closed stations, extended voting, defective procedures, opaque tabulation, military-school polling allegations, and annulled results. [BATCH-0001-E013, BATCH-0001-E016, BATCH-0005-E002, BATCH-0005-E006, BATCH-0007-E010, BATCH-0023-E024, BATCH-0013-E008, BATCH-0013-E009, BATCH-0019-E013] Conflict prevented voting in Rutshuru and Masisi and excluded hundreds of thousands, while women and other groups remained underrepresented. [BATCH-0013-E011, BATCH-0028-E011] The campaign was competitive but involved violence, ruling-coalition administrative-resource abuse, blocked opposition activity, and allegations of fraud and repression; post-election protesters demanded a rerun and were prohibited. [BATCH-0001-E014, BATCH-0002-E013, BATCH-0003-E002, BATCH-0003-E003, BATCH-0021-E009, BATCH-0010-E022] Tshisekedi was declared the winner and his coalition won 450 of 477 confirmed legislative seats, but opposition candidates disputed the process. [BATCH-0007-E001, BATCH-0028-E010, BATCH-0005-E009] These outcomes establish formal access and adjudication, not acceptance of a verified opposition victory; no opposition victory occurred. Most operational failures are attributed to CENI, courts, local authorities, ruling-party supporters, or conflict conditions rather than personally to Tshisekedi, and the record does not establish whether irregularities changed the presidential result.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E012","BATCH-0001-E015","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0027-E001","BATCH-0001-E016","BATCH-0013-E008","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0028-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E013","BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0005-E002","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0007-E010","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0019-E013","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0028-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The constitutional term-limit text and the election’s effect on voter intent are not supplied.","Personal presidential control over CENI, electoral-resource abuse, and local violence is not established.","Several observer findings, casualty accounts, and fraud allegations remain disputed or preliminary.","No opposition victory occurred, so acceptance of such a victory cannot be directly tested."]},{"question_id":"4B.2","answer":"Tshisekedi did not consistently refrain from using state authority in ways that could entrench incumbent power. Favorable evidence includes his directive to ministries, security services, CENI, courts, and tribunals to protect voters and electoral materials and punish electoral violations, CENI’s register-audit process, restoration of excluded candidacies, annulment of some disputed results including ruling-coalition candidates, and the existence of formal budget and audit safeguards. [BATCH-0009-E001, BATCH-0027-E011, BATCH-0005-E005, BATCH-0007-E007, BATCH-0029-E005] However, the state of siege was repeatedly extended by presidential instruments, transferred civilian administration to military and police authorities, replaced elected provincial institutions, restricted opposition and protest activity, and enabled military prosecution of civilians. [BATCH-0012-R03-E001, BATCH-0012-R03-E002, BATCH-0012-R03-E003, BATCH-0015-E007] Authorities blocked Katumbi’s travel and opposition sit-ins, arrested opposition figures, banned a post-election opposition march, and ruling-party supporters were implicated in attacks and sexual violence against opposition supporters. [BATCH-0003-E002, BATCH-0003-E003, BATCH-0003-E007, BATCH-0021-E009, BATCH-0002-E014] The electoral process also showed administrative-resource abuse, perceived CENI proximity to government, weak implementation of prior electoral reforms, and major logistical and tabulation irregularities. [BATCH-0001-E014, BATCH-0010-E020, BATCH-0013-E010, BATCH-0013-E009] The administration’s support for Wazalendo and FDLR, private military personnel, and armed drones increased coercive capacity, but the evidence does not prove those choices were made specifically to preserve personal or party power. [BATCH-0028-E016, BATCH-0011-E019] Direct presidential attribution is strongest for state-of-siege extensions and electoral directives; most local restrictions and abuses remain government-level or party-linked evidence rather than proof of a personal order.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-R03-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E002","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0021-E009","BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0010-E020","BATCH-0013-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0007-E007","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0028-E016","BATCH-0011-E019"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal safeguards do not establish consistent implementation or independence.","The record does not prove personal presidential direction of every irregularity, restriction, or party-linked attack.","Security measures may reflect wartime objectives rather than entrenchment, and intent is not established.","The legality and practical effect of some state-of-siege extensions remain incompletely documented."]},{"question_id":"4B.3","answer":"Protection of opposition, criticism, protest, journalism, satire, and civic monitoring was materially inadequate despite some legal and corrective measures. The revised press law guaranteed access to some non-classified public-interest information, and authorities sometimes condemned attacks, arrested officers, released Diongo without charge, and escorted a peaceful October march. [BATCH-0025-E007, BATCH-0027-E005, BATCH-0003-E007, BATCH-0022-E014, BATCH-0002-E012] In practice, police violently dispersed the May opposition march, Tshisekedi congratulated the supervising police chief, authorities blocked opposition meetings and sit-ins, detained opposition figures, and banned a post-election protest. [BATCH-0002-E011, BATCH-0003-E002, BATCH-0003-E003, BATCH-0010-E022, BATCH-0021-E009] The Goma operation against a banned protest killed at least 56 people according to the official count, while Amnesty reported a disputed higher UN estimate; civilians were arrested and subsequent investigations and trials were contested. [BATCH-0011-E018, BATCH-0011-E020, BATCH-0011-E021, BATCH-0023-E014] Journalists were arrested, beaten, threatened, denied access, or prosecuted, including Bujakera, Bakuka, Kayiba, Ngongo Lomango, and journalists attacked by ruling-party or allied supporters; the national broadcaster lacked independence and impunity remained a reported pattern. [BATCH-0025-E008, BATCH-0025-E012, BATCH-0026-E007, BATCH-0026-E011, BATCH-0027-E002, BATCH-0027-E004, BATCH-0027-E005, BATCH-0025-E011] Tshisekedi stated that criticism of human-rights violations would not change his security position, while his claimed non-intervention in Bujakera’s case showed a separation-of-powers position but not an effective remedy. [BATCH-0003-E010, BATCH-0025-E013] Some attacks involved opposition or non-state actors, and most incidents are attributed to authorities or party supporters rather than directly to Tshisekedi; final accountability is often unknown.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0011-E020","BATCH-0025-E008","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0003-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0027-E005","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0025-E013","BATCH-0011-E021"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The record does not establish a personal presidential order for most incidents.","Goma casualty figures and official investigations remain disputed or incomplete.","The effectiveness and independence of announced investigations and remedies are not established.","Some violence involved opposition supporters, armed groups, or other non-state actors."]},{"question_id":"4B.4","answer":"Courts, election bodies, legislatures, and monitoring institutions retained some operational capacity, but their independence and ability to constrain the executive were uneven. The Constitutional Court reviewed candidacies, reinstated two candidates, adjudicated electoral challenges, and CENI commissioned a mixed audit of the voter register; Parliament and the Court of Accounts later scrutinized 2023 budget execution and identified overruns, uncertified debts, emergency procedures, weak provincial allocations, and projects lacking observed field action. [BATCH-0005-E005, BATCH-0023-E015, BATCH-0017-E003, BATCH-0024-E003, BATCH-0024-E004] The National Commission on Human Rights issued reports and visited detention centers, although its effectiveness and provincial presence were limited. [BATCH-0011-E014] These are meaningful checks, but some occurred through institutional self-reporting or retrospective review and do not establish independence. Against them, presidential judicial ordinances revoked, retired, promoted, appointed, and reassigned judges and prosecutors without disclosed selection criteria; the state of siege replaced elected governors, suspended provincial assemblies, and subjected civilians to military courts. [BATCH-0015-E006, BATCH-0019-E005, BATCH-0019-E006, BATCH-0012-R03-E003] Observers reported unexplained Constitutional Court decisions, alleged corruption suspicions involving electoral judges, perceived CENI politicization, opaque tabulation, and claims that courts were subservient to power. [BATCH-0001-E016, BATCH-0008-E004, BATCH-0013-E009, BATCH-0028-E017, BATCH-0028-E018, BATCH-0028-E023] Tshisekedi said he would not intervene in Bujakera’s case, but that statement does not prove practical judicial independence. [BATCH-0025-E013] The evidence therefore supports partial institutional checking, not consistent protection of jurisdiction, appointment independence, tenure, funding, or decisions when they constrained the ruler.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0017-E003","BATCH-0024-E003","BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0011-E014","BATCH-0025-E013"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E006","BATCH-0019-E005","BATCH-0019-E006","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0001-E016","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0028-E017","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0028-E023"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Court funding, tenure protection, legislative independence, and local-government autonomy are not comprehensively documented.","Several adverse findings concern institutional perceptions or government-level conduct rather than proven presidential interference.","Fiscal oversight evidence concerns later review of 2023 execution, not contemporaneous presidential compliance.","Reasons for judicial removals and subsequent judicial performance are not supplied."]},{"question_id":"4B.5","answer":"The evidence shows formal administrative capacity-building alongside substantial politicization and loyalty risks. Budget rules required objectives, indicators, reporting, internal controls, and audit committees, while UNDP and ILO supported recruitment and training of magistrates, police investigators, and labor inspectors. [BATCH-0029-E004, BATCH-0029-E005, BATCH-0009-E004, BATCH-0023-E017] These measures establish institutional design or capacity inputs, not politically neutral appointments. Tshisekedi directly made broad judicial personnel changes, including promotions, dismissals, compulsory retirements, reassignments, and appointments across civilian and military courts, and appointed senior magistrates and prosecutors. [BATCH-0015-E006, BATCH-0019-E005, BATCH-0019-E006, BATCH-0019-E007] He also appointed managers and board chairs across public enterprises and regulatory bodies, reshuffled the cabinet, and appointed Gécamines leadership, but the supplied records provide no selection criteria, qualifications, tenure safeguards, or performance results. [BATCH-0008-E014, BATCH-0009-E003, BATCH-0018-E004] Independent reporting described the judiciary and CENI as politically close to the government or perceived as politicized, including concerns about the CENI chair and sympathetic judicial appointments. [BATCH-0010-E020, BATCH-0028-E021, BATCH-0028-E018] Government rhetoric also emphasized presidential authority and loyalty to the nation, but the record does not establish systematic loyalty tests or a personality cult. [BATCH-0012-R09-E002, BATCH-0019-E010] Attribution is strongest for presidential ordinances and appointments; broader institutional dysfunction, patronage, and alleged capture remain partly inferential or institution-level.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E006","BATCH-0019-E005","BATCH-0019-E006","BATCH-0019-E007","BATCH-0008-E014","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0010-E020"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E004","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0023-E017","BATCH-0028-E021","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0012-R09-E002","BATCH-0019-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Selection criteria, qualifications, tenure, party ties, and performance are missing for most appointees.","Formal training and administrative rules do not establish neutrality in practice.","Reports of politicization include perceptions and allegations rather than complete adjudicated findings.","Systematic loyalty tests, a personality cult, and direct personal responsibility for every institutional failure are not established."]},{"question_id":"4B.6","answer":"The information environment was governed by a mixed formal framework but was substantially pressured in practice. The April 2023 press-law revision guaranteed access to some non-classified public-interest information, while retaining possible imprisonment for press offenses, a bad-faith false-information clause, and state-security and national-defense exclusions. [BATCH-0025-E007] The government also invited election observers, CENI announced a mixed external register audit, and the state did not have a supplied finding of a nationwide internet shutdown or online-content censorship regime. [BATCH-0028-E007, BATCH-0027-E011, BATCH-0011-E011] Conversely, RSF reported an independent-media environment weakened by pressure from politicians, local authorities, militias, and religious groups, an insufficiently independent national broadcaster, journalist arrests, threats, disappearances, and attacks; it ranked the DRC 130th of 180 in its 2023 index, while Tshisekedi’s claimed improvement was self-reported and not independently substantiated here. [BATCH-0025-E008, BATCH-0025-E026, BATCH-0022-E006] Journalists were arrested or attacked during the campaign, including Bujakera, FARDC-beaten journalists, journalists targeted by UDPS or allied supporters, and reporters denied access; CSAC also ordered Perfect Télévision off air after election reporting. [BATCH-0025-E012, BATCH-0026-E007, BATCH-0027-E002, BATCH-0027-E003, BATCH-0027-E004] OLPA reported that provincial media regulation was under-resourced and weak, creating conditions for disinformation and ethnic hate speech. [BATCH-0006-E009] The EU mission was reduced to an eight-person expert mission, but the supplied EEAS record does not establish why; HRW separately reports that authorities did not authorize satellite equipment. [BATCH-0028-E003, BATCH-0002-E018] The evidence therefore supports limited formal openness and some regulatory correction, but not a reliably independent information system. Personal presidential direction of individual media abuses is generally not established.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0025-E008","BATCH-0025-E026","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0027-E002","BATCH-0027-E003","BATCH-0006-E009","BATCH-0002-E018"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E007","BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0022-E006","BATCH-0028-E003","BATCH-0027-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The press-law text, enforcement, and judicial interpretation are not fully supplied.","The record does not establish presidential control over CENI, CSAC, the broadcaster, or individual journalist cases.","The cause of the EU mission reduction is unresolved.","No complete evidence is supplied on media ownership, funding, or final remedies for attacks and shutdowns."]},{"question_id":"4B.7","answer":"The government enacted or maintained some formal inclusion measures, but equal political access in practice remained substantially unequal. Tshisekedi signed the Indigenous Peoples’ rights law; the victim-reparation framework provided legal assistance, protection, health care, compensation, and guarantees of non-repetition; and 2023 justice and gender-related measures included laws on human-rights defenders, sexual-violence reparations, trafficking, and penitentiary principles. [BATCH-0001-E010, BATCH-0029-E001, BATCH-0029-E002, BATCH-0009-E004] Elections permitted diaspora voting, broad party registration, and citizen observation, but voter education and registration did not fully reach women, Indigenous people, persons with disabilities, or internally displaced people; polling infrastructure was inaccessible, women won only 61 of 477 initially confirmed legislative seats, and voting did not occur in conflict-affected territories. [BATCH-0001-E013, BATCH-0001-E015, BATCH-0023-E023, BATCH-0028-E011, BATCH-0013-E011] Opposition candidates and supporters faced blocked rallies, arrests, restrictions on movement, ruling-party-linked violence, sexual violence in Kasumbalesa, and exclusionary ethnic-regional rhetoric by aligned governors. [BATCH-0003-E002, BATCH-0003-E003, BATCH-0003-E007, BATCH-0002-E014, BATCH-0002-E017, BATCH-0006-E004] Women, ethnic minorities, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, and LGBT+ people continued to face discrimination and violence; enforcement and services were generally weak, including very low schooling access for children with disabilities. [BATCH-0002-E022, BATCH-0011-E015, BATCH-0026-E010] Some regulatory and government responses were favorable, but implementation, funding, geographic reach, and presidential causation are incompletely established; conflict and armed-group control explain part, but not all, of the exclusion.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E010","BATCH-0029-E001","BATCH-0029-E002","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0001-E013","BATCH-0023-E023","BATCH-0028-E011","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0003-E002","BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0002-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E015","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0020-E007","BATCH-0022-E010","BATCH-0026-E009","BATCH-0026-E010","BATCH-0020-E015","BATCH-0020-E016","BATCH-0020-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal laws and programs do not establish effective enforcement or equal practical access.","Many outcomes are attributable to institutions, conflict, armed groups, structural inequality, or international partners rather than directly to Tshisekedi.","Complete disaggregated data for minorities, women, opposition regions, and unpopular viewpoints are unavailable.","The record does not establish whether Tshisekedi endorsed or remedied exclusionary statements by aligned officials."]},{"question_id":"4B.8","answer":"Tshisekedi remained within the scheduled formal succession process insofar as he sought a second term, elections were held, and the Constitutional Court later confirmed his reelection; no supplied evidence establishes a constitutional term-limit amendment or formal violation. [BATCH-0005-E008, BATCH-0015-E001, BATCH-0018-E006] However, compliance with formal timing did not establish a credible, impartial transfer framework. The election involved delayed and extended voting, nonvoting in conflict-affected territories, disputed tabulation, annulled constituencies, violence, low turnout, perceived politicization of CENI and the Court, and opposition rejection of the results. [BATCH-0013-E011, BATCH-0028-E011, BATCH-0013-E009, BATCH-0028-E018, BATCH-0007-E007] Tshisekedi’s coalition won 450 of 477 confirmed legislative seats, while women initially won only 61 seats, indicating dominant coalition control and limited representation but not by itself a succession violation. [BATCH-0028-E010, BATCH-0028-E011] A Tshisekedi political coordinator urged rival camps to accept the results, and the Court reviewed challenges, but neither establishes a personal presidential acceptance of a verified opposition victory; none occurred. [BATCH-0006-E006, BATCH-0007-E001] The CENCO-ECC mission identified anomalies and urged corrective compilation, while post-election opposition protests seeking a rerun were banned. [BATCH-0005-E006, BATCH-0021-E009] The evidence therefore supports formal continuity of elections and succession procedures, but not robust proof that transfer safeguards were independent, fully credible, or tested against an adverse result.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E008","BATCH-0015-E001","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0007-E001","BATCH-0006-E006","BATCH-0028-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0028-E011","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0007-E007","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0021-E009"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The applicable constitutional term-limit provision is not supplied, so legal compliance cannot be independently tested.","The Court’s confirmation is an institutional ruling, not an independent election-integrity assessment.","No opposition victory occurred, leaving acceptance of adverse transfer untested.","Post-election events and allegations are partly retrospective, disputed, or outside the target-year boundary."]},{"question_id":"4B.9","answer":"The evidence does not establish presidential procurement or operation of spyware, a targeted interception system, or a nationwide internet shutdown; one 2023 government assessment expressly reported no internet restriction, disruption, or online-content censorship. [BATCH-0011-E011] Nevertheless, political freedom was constrained through legal and administrative controls. The Digital Code carried prison penalties for disseminating false information, and the revised press law retained imprisonment for press offenses and a bad-faith false-information provision. [BATCH-0011-E011, BATCH-0025-E007] Authorities detained journalists over alleged false information or security reporting, including Bujakera, Bakuka, Kayiba, and Ngongo Lomango; phones were retained in one case, and critics, satirists, opposition figures, and activists were arrested or searched. [BATCH-0025-E011, BATCH-0025-E012, BATCH-0026-E011, BATCH-0010-E013, BATCH-0003-E006] The state of siege, repeatedly extended under presidential ordinances, transferred authority to military and police officials and was associated with harassment and detention of critics, journalists, activists, and opposition members. [BATCH-0012-R03-E001, BATCH-0012-R03-E002, BATCH-0012-R03-E003, BATCH-0015-E007] Protest bans and force, including the Goma operation, further show coercive suppression, while the CENI audit terms and EU observation arrangements provide qualifying evidence of some procedural oversight. [BATCH-0011-E018, BATCH-0027-E011, BATCH-0028-E007] Tshisekedi’s roundtable on whether to maintain, requalify, or lift the state of siege and his stated non-intervention in Bujakera’s case were limited corrective signals, not demonstrated remedies. [BATCH-0021-E012, BATCH-0025-E013] Most conduct is attributed to agencies or security forces rather than a personal presidential order, and the absence of evidence of shutdowns or spyware does not negate the documented use of criminal law, detention, and administrative pressure.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0025-E011","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0010-E013","BATCH-0012-R03-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E002","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0011-E018"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0027-E011","BATCH-0028-E007","BATCH-0021-E012","BATCH-0025-E013","BATCH-0022-E006","BATCH-0027-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No surveillance procurement, interception, shutdown, or data-access record is supplied.","Legal restrictions on online speech are distinct from surveillance and shutdown controls, and the record should not conflate them.","The state-of-siege transition and announced investigations were not shown to be fully implemented or independently effective.","Casualty figures and some security accounts remain disputed."]},{"question_id":"4B.10","answer":"The evidence does not establish that Tshisekedi left political freedom and democratic resilience durably stronger than inherited. Favorable evidence includes elections held on schedule, a CENI-commissioned five-member mixed national-international register audit, formal rights and justice legislation, recruitment and training of magistrates, selected justice outputs, a 12% decline in documented human-rights violations, some fiscal and institutional oversight, and limited media or protest safeguards. [BATCH-0001-E012, BATCH-0023-E015, BATCH-0009-E004, BATCH-0011-E003, BATCH-0025-E009, BATCH-0024-E003, BATCH-0022-E014] These are evidence of formal acts or partial outputs, but the audit was reported by CENI, justice results were materially partner-supported, the human-rights decline may reflect reporting and conflict conditions, and durability or independent reviewability is not shown. Against this, the state of siege displaced elected civilian institutions and was associated with serious abuses; opposition and journalists faced restrictions and violence; the 2023 election had major logistical, transparency, participation, and credibility defects; prior electoral reforms were reportedly not implemented; CENI and the Constitutional Court remained perceived as politicized; and transitional-justice commitments did not produce concrete measures. [BATCH-0012-R03-E003, BATCH-0012-R03-E004, BATCH-0012-R03-E007, BATCH-0028-E014, BATCH-0028-E018, BATCH-0013-E010, BATCH-0010-E016, BATCH-0028-E017] Campaign and post-election violence, administrative-resource abuse, party-linked attacks, conflict-related disenfranchisement, and weak remedies further burdened resilience. [BATCH-0001-E014, BATCH-0002-E013, BATCH-0026-E012, BATCH-0013-E011] Conflict, armed groups, regional intervention, donor involvement, inherited institutional weakness, and limited post-period evidence constrain causation. The balance supports some formal reform and partial institutional capacity, but not durable ruler-attributable strengthening of contestability, civic space, independent constraints, or democratic resilience.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E012","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0025-E009","BATCH-0024-E003","BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0010-E016"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0012-R03-E004","BATCH-0012-R03-E007","BATCH-0028-E014","BATCH-0028-E018","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0028-E017","BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0013-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal laws, staffing, audits, and selected outputs do not establish independent reviewability, nationwide implementation, or durability.","Many adverse findings concern government institutions or security forces collectively rather than proven personal presidential direction.","The 12% decline in documented violations is not a complete measure of actual violations or democratic resilience.","Durability cannot be established without evidence extending beyond the 2023 target period.","The record lacks a counterfactual showing how political freedom would have evolved without Tshisekedi."]}],"cross_lens_observations":["The strongest ruler-attributable evidence concerns state-of-siege continuation, presidential judicial personnel actions, public security rhetoric, and formal electoral or institutional directives; many operational failures and abuses remain attributable only to government bodies, security forces, parties, or conflict conditions.","Formal legal and administrative activity coexisted with weak implementation, contested institutional independence, opposition repression, media pressure, and unresolved accountability.","The election and state-of-siege record are consequential across multiple lenses, but the supplied evidence does not establish personal presidential intent or causation for every adverse event.","Some favorable evidence shows correction, oversight, inclusion, or capacity-building, but generally not durable, independently verified strengthening." ]}
